root_cause.text: The omap_dma_probe() function fails to release the dma_pool (created via dma_pool_create()) in error paths when dma_async_device_register() or of_dma_controller_register() fails, causing a resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `dma_pool_destroy(od->desc_pool)` in both error paths (after failed `dma_async_device_register()` and after failed `of_dma_controller_register()`), as shown in the diff. The commit message explicitly states: "The dma_pool created by dma_pool_create() is not destroyed when dma_async_device_register() or of_dma_controller_register() fails, causing a resource leak in the probe error paths."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak of DMA descriptor pool in omap_dma_probe error path by calling dma_pool_destroy when ll123_supported is true.
intent_record.what: Added conditional call to dma_pool_destroy(od->desc_pool) when od->ll123_supported is true, before omap_dma_free(od) in the error path of omap_dma_probe.
intent_record.how: This ensures the descriptor pool is explicitly freed when registration of slave DMA engine fails and the hardware supports ll123, preventing a memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak by destroying DMA descriptor pool when DMA controller registration fails on OMAP platforms with LL123 support.
intent_record.what: Added conditional dma_pool_destroy call for descriptor pool when DMA controller registration fails and LL123 is supported.
intent_record.how: Ensures the descriptor pool (od->desc_pool) is destroyed before freeing the DMA device structure, preventing a memory leak in the error path of omap_dma_probe when registration fails.
